fr.recommendations:
• Install reflective address numbers visible from the street at the driveway entrance.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the driveway to maintain clear vehicle passage from the street to the parking area.
• Mark the rear access point with a reflective sign or post so responders can locate it quickly from outside the property.
• Keep the rear access gate unlocked or secured with a breakaway lock to allow responders to reach the back of the property without delay.
• Cut back dense vegetation along walkways so responders can move on foot between the front and sides of the house without obstruction.
• Clear a path wide enough for a responder carrying equipment between the main residence and the detached structure.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear enough that emergency vehicles can turn around or stage near the house.
• Mark all access points in the perimeter fencing so responders arriving from any side can quickly identify entry locations.
• Thin dense plantings near the detached structure so responders can approach and work around it without pushing through heavy growth.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim lower branches on scattered trees near structures to reduce the chance of fire climbing from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Thin trees within the cluster closest to any structure to create more open space between individual trees.
• Remove or cut back shrubs that are growing directly against or touching any part of the structure.
• Keep shrubs near the structure trimmed low and separated from one another to reduce the chance of fire spreading between them.
• Maintain the open green space by mowing or cutting grass regularly to keep it short, especially during dry periods.
• Keep both access routes clear of overhanging branches and low-growing vegetation along the edges of the driveway or road.
• Remove any dead branches or accumulated dead plant material from beneath trees near the structure.
• Maintain the existing open separation between vegetation and structures by not adding new plantings, woodpiles, or stored materials in those cleared areas.
